question.problem:
The local truncation error (LTE) of a numerical method with step size $Δx$ is

$$
τ(Δx)=3(Δx)^{3}+2(Δx)^{4}.
$$

Complete the following sentences.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.8,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.2,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Decreasing from $Δx=0.8$ to $Δx=0.2,$ the LTE is reduced by a factor of $≈$
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ According to this data, the order of the method is approximately
{{field-4}}.
question.worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies

$$
τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p+1})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p+1}.$

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

- With step size $Δx=0.8,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.8) & =3(0.8)^{3}+2(0.8)^{4} \\  & =3\cdot 0.512+2\cdot 0.409\,6 \\  & =1.536+0.819\,2 \\  & =2.355\,2 \\  & ≈2.355.\end{aligned}
$$

- With step size $Δx=0.2,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.2) & =3(0.2)^{3}+2(0.2)^{4} \\  & =3\cdot 0.008+2\cdot 0.001\,6 \\  & =0.024+0.003\,2 \\  & =0.027\,2 \\  & ≈0.027.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from $0.8$ to $0.2.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.8}{0.2}=4.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p+1}={4}^{p+1}.
$$

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from $2.355\,2$ to $0.027\,2.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{2.355\,2}{0.027\,2}=86.588\,23…≈86.588.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{p+1} & ≈86.588\,23… \\ p+1 & ≈{log}_{4}⁡(86.588\,23…) \\ p+1 & ≈3.218… \\ p & ≈2.218….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is
$2.$

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE:

$$
τ(Δx)=3(Δx)^{3}+2(Δx)^{4}\,⇒\,τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{3})=O\,((Δx)^{2+1}),\,Δx\to 0.
$$

Hence, the order of the method is $2.$
